ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD shaped like a kite, with A on the left, B at the top, C on the right, and D at the bottom. The side markings show AB and AD each have one tick mark, so AB = AD, while BC and CD each have two tick marks, so BC = CD. The angle at A is labeled 74°, the angle at D is labeled 105°, and the angle at C is labeled x°. Reasoning: Since AB = AD, BC = CD, and AC is a shared side, triangles ABC and ADC are congruent by SSS. Therefore the corresponding angles at B and D are equal, so ∠B = ∠D = 105°. The angles of quadrilateral ABCD sum to 360°, so 74 + 105 + x + 105 = 360. Thus x = 360 - 284 = 76. Therefore m∠C = 76°.

method.method_draft: Read from the image that ABCD is a kite with adjacent equal pairs AB = AD and BC = CD, and that ∠A = 74°, ∠D = 105°, while ∠C is x°. Since in this kite the diagonal AC connects the vertices where the equal side pairs meet, AC is the symmetry diagonal and bisects the angles at A and C. Thus in triangle ADC, the angle at A is half of 74°, namely 37°, and the angle at C is half of x. Use the triangle angle sum in triangle ADC: 37 + 105 + x/2 = 180. Then x/2 = 38, so x = 76.
